🌍 LIVE EARTH MONITORING REPORT
🛰️ https://t.co/O8uWWmbiJj — Real-time seismic & volcanic watch
Today’s earthquakes are clustering along the Pacific Ring of Fire, directly linked to major volcanic systems. Below is a location-by-location correlation ⬇️

🔥 BANDA SEA — M5.4 EARTHQUAKE
📍 Deep tectonic zone, Indonesia

Nearest volcanoes:
• 🌋 Banda Api — active volcanic island
• 🌋 Mount Nila — historical eruptions
• 🌋 Mount Wurlali (Damar Island) — active stratovolcano
🧠 Cause: Subduction of the Indo-Australian Plate beneath the Banda Arc
⚠️ Note: Earthquakes here often precede volcanic unrest

🔥 PHILIPPINES — M5.0 EARTHQUAKE (SE of Pondaguitan)
Nearest active volcanoes:
• 🌋 Mount Kanlaon — erupted in 2025
• 🌋 Mount Mayon — one of the world’s most active
• 🌋 Mount Bulusan — frequent ash emissions
• 🌋 Mount Pinatubo — historically explosive
🧠 Cause: Complex collision of Philippine Sea Plate & Eurasian Plate
⚠️ High volcano density zone
🌋 CALIFORNIA, USA — Multiple Small Quakes

Nearest volcanic systems:
• 🌋 The Geysers Geothermal Field
• 🌋 Clear Lake Volcanic Field
• 🌋 Long Valley Caldera (regional influence)
🧠 Cause: San Andreas Fault system
ℹ️ Mostly tectonic, but geothermal activity present

❄️ ALASKA — M2.2 (SW of Susitna)

Nearest volcanoes:
• 🌋 Mount Spurr
• 🌋 Mount Redoubt
• 🌋 Mount Iliamna
🧠 Cause: Pacific Plate subducting under North American Plate
⚠️ One of Earth’s most active volcano-earthquake regions
🌊 PUERTO RICO — M2.5 (Las Marías)
Nearest volcanic feature:
• 🌋 Puerto Rico Trench (submarine system)
🧠 Cause: Caribbean–North American Plate boundary
ℹ️ Mostly tectonic, limited surface volcanism

📡 SPACE TRACKER INSIGHT
Earthquakes and volcanoes are not random — they are surface signals of deep planetary mechanics.
Where plates collide, magma rises.
We are monitoring these zones live.
